title: The trip of a radio message
instruction: Put in order what happens from pressing the button to the heart on the other micro:bit.
steps: The micro:bit wraps the number 1 in a packet with group 7
The radio sends the packet out around it
micro:bits in group 7 receive it, the others throw it away
The receiving micro:bit shows a heart
debrief: A radio message is a small packet with a group. Only micro:bits in the same group and in range receive it.
why: An event: pressing the button starts the sending.
The message travels as a packet, and the group is its address.
The radio broadcasts to everyone in range; there is no router in between.
The group tells who the packet belongs to.
Only after receiving it does the “on radio received number” handler run.
